show_hn.story_text: I made an agent-native 3d/vfx engine. Agents are good at making interesting scenes in Blender/Unreal/Nuke/etc. But these tools are fundamentally limited compared to what coding agents are capable of. In vork, agents write the whole scene as code, including their own shaders, materials, cameras and physics, and vork renders it on the GPU. The core API fits in about 2,500 tokens. So, for example, almost every 3d engine assumes light moves in a straight line. Light near a black hole does not; so the best you can do in e.g. Blender is faking gravitational lensing. show_hn.story_text: I built the first version of this stuff a decade ago as ethanolus (c2h5oh). And I've used it for most of my projects as a backend layer since then. The main motive is to eliminate unnecessary complexity from backend layers. How it works: a rust nginx module calls postgresql functions via non-blocking libpq io. Realtime listen/notify updates from postgres without polling. How to try - code on github. Tested on Debian - FreeBSD validation in progress. It's alpha - so any feedback is welcome.

I came up with a new approach: by patching rapydscript-ng (a tool that transpiles Python-like syntax to JS), I make it translate Manim code into JS, and pair it with a companion JS library. This lets it run the original code in a small enough bundle. Fortunately, after overcoming some difficulties, it worked! It runs surprisingly well. Show HN: MyBox – Isolate your projects in a Linux box
show_hn.story_text: Hi HN, I’ve built MyBox to isolate my development projects in Linux containers. Installing npm modules on my machine didn’t feel right anymore. MyBox is built on a fork of apple/container. - Each box has its own Linux kernel. - Project files get copied into the box (no folder mounts). - Packet filtering blocks access to the Mac and local network (internet access from the box is allowed). - Mac apps cannot reach into the box (a dedicated macOS account owns the runtime and virtual disks). - Touch ID or a password is required to access the box (e.g. opening a shell, importing & exporting files). I started with a CLI tool, but for convenience I’ve built a desktop app around it. <a href="https://github.com/janpmz/mybox" rel="nofollow">https://github.com&#x
